title: The Peloponnesian War
objective: After this level you can explain why Athens and Sparta fought for 27 years.
summary: From 431 to 404 BCE Athens’s navy fought Sparta’s army; Thucydides blamed Spartan fear of Athens. Plague hit Athens, and Sparta, with Persian aid, won.

cards.headline: The Greeks who beat Persia together fought each other for 27 years.
cards.body: And at the end, Persia helped decide who won.

cards.headline: Sea power against land power
cards.body: From 431 to 404 BCE Athens, leading the Delian League, fought Sparta, leading the Peloponnesian League. Athens had the stronger navy; Sparta’s alliance had the stronger army on land. Thucydides, who lived through the war and wrote its history, said the real cause was Athens’s growing power and the fear it caused in Sparta.

cards.headline: Safe behind the walls
cards.body: Under Pericles, Athens avoided Sparta’s army, kept its people inside the city walls and relied on its navy. Then, in 430 BCE, plague struck the crowded city. It killed tens of thousands, including Pericles. Thucydides caught it too, and survived to write about it. The plan to stay safe had packed everyone together for the disease.

cards.headline: Persian gold, Spartan ships
cards.body: Athens lost a huge expedition to Sicily in 415–413 BCE. Then, in 405 BCE, the Spartan admiral Lysander, with much aid from Persia, destroyed the Athenian fleet at Aegospotami. Athens surrendered in 404 BCE. Persia had lost to the Greeks at Salamis. In the end, it helped sink Athens anyway.

cards.fact: Athens’s walls came down to flute music.
cards.context: Xenophon says the victors tore them down to the music of flute girls, thinking that day the beginning of freedom for Greece. The Delian League was disbanded the same year.

questions.prompt: What struck crowded Athens in 430 BCE and killed Pericles?

options.label: A Spartan siege
options.rationale: Sparta’s army stayed outside the walls.

questions.explanation: In 430 BCE plague struck Athens, crowded inside its walls, killing tens of thousands, including Pericles.

questions.prompt: According to Thucydides, what was the real cause of the war between Athens and Sparta?

options.label: A quarrel over the Olympic Games
options.rationale: He pointed to power and fear.

options.label: Athens’s growing power and Sparta’s fear of it
A Persian plot to split the Greeks
A dispute over who owned Delos
options.rationale: He pointed to power and fear.

questions.explanation: Thucydides said the growth of Athenian power and the fear it caused in Sparta made the war.

questions.prompt: Persia’s fleet lost at Salamis in Level 37. What part did Persia play at the end of the Peloponnesian War?

options.label: It fought for Athens at Aegospotami
It stayed out of Greek affairs
It aided Sparta’s fleet against Athens
It conquered both Athens and Sparta
